title: Ouray City Council Regular Meeting
location: Ouray Community Center, 320 6th Ave, Ouray, CO 81427
summary: A full agenda for Ouray, which marks its 150th anniversary at this meeting. The consequential items: first readings of two ordinances — one setting 2027 water and sewer rates, and one addressing Light Industrial zoning and EQR (equivalent residential unit) calculations. Council also takes up Resolution No. 23, an intergovernmental agreement with the Ouray County Sheriff for full law-enforcement services — a structural decision about how the city gets policed. Resolution No. 24 covers a water service termination agreement. A perimeter trail easement request and a Responsible Entity Agreement round out the action items. On the discussion side, Waterview Phase II rural homes gets a council direction conversation, with the 2024 housing needs analysis and strategy addendum in the packet. Home Trust of Ouray County presents its quarterly housing services report.

title: Planning and Zoning Commission Meeting
location: 1670 Naturita St, Norwood CO 81423
summary: Norwood's Planning and Zoning Commission meets October 19 at 6:30 p.m. at Town Hall. Two substantive items anchor the session: a Land Use Code Update and a Master Plan Update — both the kind of foundational work that shapes what gets built where, and under what rules, for years to come. The board will also address a Board Seat Update. Consent agenda covers September 21 minutes.

title: Board of Directors Meeting
location: 131 W Columbia Ave, Telluride, CO 81435
summary: The Telluride Fire Protection District board meets October 20th at 5:30 p.m. at Station 1 on Columbia Ave. Leading the agenda is the first reading of the 2027 budget — the opening move in a process that will play out over the next several weeks. The board will also ratify a pre-build contractor agreement with FCI, likely tied to the ongoing Station 3 update, and will receive a wildfire assignment update along with a September report on PANO camera usage. On a brighter note, the district is set to recognize an EMS Excellence in Quality Care and Data Reporting award from CDPHE. Staff reports from the Deputy Chief, Battalion Chief, Fire Marshal, EMS Coordinator, HR Coordinator, and District Chief round out the evening. No executive session is scheduled.

title: Telluride Board of Education Monthly Meeting
location: Bridal Veil District Conference Room / Zoom
summary: The October 20 meeting has a full plate. On the action side, the board votes to approve the Unified Improvement Plan and a resolution recognizing Principal Appreciation Month. Discussion items carry more weight: the MLO and funding update returns — the mill levy override has been a recurring thread through recent meetings, and board members have been doing their own outreach to voters. There's also a housing update, which connects to the district's ongoing effort to build rental and for-sale units at Two Rivers using remaining bond funds — 14 rental and 6 for-sale units were the figures on the table last month. The Unified Improvement Plan gets both discussion time and a formal vote. The board will also work through the student representative process and timeline, CASB planning follow-up, and a TES/TIS school report focused on the ELG Grant. Routine consent items include the September 30 quarterly financials and personnel report.

title: Board of County Commissioners Meeting
location: 333 West Colorado Ave, 2nd floor, Telluride, CO 81435
summary: The headline work here is a suite of four Land Use Code amendments that would add an entirely new Article 6 — Natural Resources — to San Miguel County's code. Three sections get individual public hearings: forestry practices (Section 6-4), oil and gas operations (Section 6-5), and deep geothermal operations (also called Section 6-4 in the agenda, likely a numbering error to watch). A fourth resolution then amends Articles 1, 3, 4, and 5 to align existing code with the new natural-resources framework. That's a significant rewrite of how the county regulates extraction and land management. On the consent agenda: a 2027 Gondola IGA supplement and the Lawson Hill Connector Trail construction agreement. Afternoon items include a possible co-sponsorship of a CDBG grant application to restore water supply to Telluride Pines HOA residents, the 2027 Community Support Funding allocation, a $12,000 food bank request from West End Family Link, and a Public Health strategic plan presentation.

title: Parks & Recreation Commission
location: Hybrid/Rebekah Hall, 113 W Columbia Ave
summary: Two substantive action items headline this meeting. First, SBG Productions is asking to restore the Telluride Jazz Festival to a full three-day run — August 13–15, 2027 — after the 2026 event was trimmed to two days in an attempt to cut costs and boost ticket sales; that experiment didn't move the needle, and the 50th anniversary year is the occasion for returning to the traditional format. Commission approval here is a prerequisite before CCAASE takes it up on November 4, followed by Town Council. If fully approved, the festival could draw up to 6,000 people per day, with the Town collecting admissions fees of $4.15 per ticket sold — up to $63,495 for the three-day run. Second, the Commission considers a design concept for expanding the basketball court in Town Park at its existing location. The work session covers seasonal check-ins with the Telluride Soccer Club and Telluride Lacrosse Club. Staff will also brief the Commission on the 2026 project update, 2027 budget, and the upcoming winter season.

title: HARC Meeting
location: Rebekah Hall, 113 W Columbia Ave
summary: The October 21 HARC meeting is anchored by the Shandoka Lot Redevelopment Project — the Town of Telluride's own large-scale development at 860 Black Bear Rd, zoned Accommodations 2. HARC takes up Buildings 1 and 2 as one public hearing item and Buildings 3 and 4 as a second, both continued from August 19. Each application covers new construction outside the Telluride Historic Landmark District exceeding 5,000 square feet of floor area under LUC 7-203.B.2.a.1. Also on the agenda: a payment-in-lieu of parking request for one space at 510 W Columbia Ave/129 N Townsend in the Historic Residential zone, where HARC is asked to support administrative approval. A small-scale new construction application at 785 Primrose Lane on a steep site is also up for review. The 448 Tomboy Road item has been continued to December 16 at the applicant's request, and the 214 S Fir Certificate of Appropriateness Amendment #2 — in the works since at least December 2025 — is being tabled for eight more months.

title: Board of Adjustment Meeting
location: 333 West Colorado Avenue, 2nd floor meeting room, Telluride, Co 81435
summary: The San Miguel County Board of Adjustment meets October 22 with one substantive item: a variance request from a Mountain Village parcel (Parcel #456536200023) to reduce the required setback from County Road 63L right-of-way. Board members will visit the site — located across from the County Jail — at 9 a.m. before convening. Approval of October 2025 minutes is also on the agenda. The meeting opens with a moment of silence for Jim Botenhagen.

title: Planning & Zoning Commission
location: Hybrid/Rebekah Hall, 113 W Columbia Ave
summary: The October 22 P&Z meeting carries two items of broader public consequence. First, the Shandoka Lot Redevelopment — a Preliminary PUD application for Town-owned property at 860 Black Bear Rd — finally gets its hearing after being continued from the September 24 meeting due to staff capacity. The proposal would increase certain dimensional limitations in exchange for public benefits on the 4.07-acre Accommodations 2-zoned parcel. Second, a Minor Subdivision at 238 North Pine Street has been making the rounds since February; the applicant now requests it be tabled another eight months. A work session on a proposed four-lot commercial subdivision at 216 & 222 W San Juan Avenue rounds out the evening.
